You solve tasks by breaking down problems into sub-tasks, writing and executing code, observing results, and iterating one step at a time.

## Prime-Agent System Prompt (ACP Template)

For file editing operations, the prime-agent runtime exposes a pre-installed `mcp` Python object with `list_tools` and `call_tool` methods. Use them to discover and invoke tools.

Example discovery and call:

```python
tools_list = await mcp.list_tools("tools")
for t in tools_list:
    print(t["name"], t["inputSchema"])

result = await mcp.call_tool("tools", "ox-bridge-write", {"path": "/tmp/x.py", "content": "# code here"})
print(result)
```

The `tools` MCP server exposes:
- `ox-bridge-write`: write a file (args: `path`, `content`)
- `ox-bridge-edit`: edit a file with hunks (args: `path`, `edits` = [{old, new}])
- `ox-bridge-read`: read a file region (args: `path`, `start`, `end`)

All bridging calls return synchronously. Print results to confirm before proceeding.

Node stdlib only: serve.js --port 0 --root DIR is a static file server with an extension map for html, css, js, json, png content types, index.html or a generated listing for directory requests, 404 for unknown paths, HEAD support, and hard path-traversal protection: any request resolving outside root (including encoded forms like %2e%2e) gets 403. Print the actually bound port on startup. Write test.sh, a bash script using curl against a fixture tree that asserts status codes and Content-Type headers for every case above plus body equality for one file, exiting nonzero on any failure. Run it and show it passing.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test.sh — exercise serve.js with curl against a fixture tree.
# Asserts status codes, Content-Type headers, HEAD support,
# directory listing/index behavior, and body equality for one file.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

PASS=0
FAIL=0

check() {
  local desc="$1" expected="$2" actual="$3"
  if [ "$actual" = "$expected" ]; then
    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
    echo "ok:   $desc (got $actual)"
  else
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
    echo "FAIL: $desc"
    echo "      expected: [$expected]"
    echo "      actual:   [$actual]"
  fi
}

# check_status DESC URL EXPECTED_STATUS [extra curl args...]
check_status() {
  local desc="$1" url="$2" want="$3"
  shift 3
  local got
  got=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$@" "$url")
  check "$desc" "$want" "$got"
}

# check_type DESC URL EXPECTED_CONTENT_TYPE
check_type() {
  local desc="$1" url="$2" want="$3"
  local got
  got=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{content_type}' "$url")
  check "$desc" "$want" "$got"
}

# --- fixture tree -----------------------------------------------------------
FIXTURE=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$FIXTURE"' EXIT

mkdir -p "$FIXTURE/www/sub/emptydir"
printf '<!DOCTYPE html><html><body>hello</body></html>\n' > "$FIXTURE/www/index.html"
printf 'body { color: red; }\n' > "$FIXTURE/www/style.css"
printf 'console.log("hi");\n' > "$FIXTURE/www/app.js"
printf '{"key": "value"}\n' > "$FIXTURE/www/data.json"
printf '\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\nfakepngdata\n' > "$FIXTURE/www/logo.png"
printf 'the quick brown fox\n' > "$FIXTURE/www/file.txt"
printf 'sub index\n' > "$FIXTURE/www/sub/index.html"
printf 'secret\n' > "$FIXTURE/outside-secret.txt"

# --- start server -----------------------------------------------------------
PORT_FILE=$(mktemp)
node serve.js --port 0 --root "$FIXTURE/www" > "$PORT_FILE" &
SERVER_PID=$!
trap 'rm -rf "$FIXTURE" "$PORT_FILE"; kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null' EXIT

for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
  [ -s "$PORT_FILE" ] && break
  sleep 0.1
done
if ! grep -qE 'port [0-9]+' "$PORT_FILE"; then
  echo "FAIL: server did not print bound port: $(cat "$PORT_FILE")"
  exit 1
fi
echo "server said: $(cat "$PORT_FILE")"

PORT=$(grep -oE '[0-9]+$' "$PORT_FILE")
BASE="http://127.0.0.1:$PORT"

# --- content types for known extensions --------------------------------------
check_type "GET /index.html -> text/html"        "$BASE/index.html" "text/html"
check_type "GET /style.css  -> text/css"         "$BASE/style.css"  "text/css"
check_type "GET /app.js     -> text/javascript"  "$BASE/app.js"     "text/javascript"
check_type "GET /data.json  -> application/json" "$BASE/data.json"  "application/json"
check_type "GET /logo.png   -> image/png"        "$BASE/logo.png"   "image/png"

# --- body equality for one file ----------------------------------------------
BODY=$(curl -s "$BASE/file.txt")
check "body of /file.txt matches fixture" "the quick brown fox" "$BODY"

# --- root directory serves index.html ----------------------------------------
check_status "GET / serves index.html"          "$BASE/" 200
check_type   "GET / has Content-Type text/html" "$BASE/" "text/html"
BODY=$(curl -s "$BASE/")
check "GET / returns index.html body" "<!DOCTYPE html><html><body>hello</body></html>" "$BODY"

# --- generated listing for directory without index.html ----------------------
check_status "GET /emptydir/ generates listing"          "$BASE/emptydir/" 200
check_type   "listing Content-Type is text/html"          "$BASE/emptydir/" "text/html"
BODY=$(curl -s "$BASE/emptydir/")
case "$BODY" in
  *Index\ of*)
    PASS=$((PASS + 1)); echo "ok:   emptydir listing contains 'Index of'"
    ;;
  *)
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); echo "FAIL: emptydir listing missing 'Index of': [$BODY]"
    ;;
esac
# subdirectory WITH an index.html must serve the index, not a listing
BODY=$(curl -s "$BASE/sub/")
check "GET /sub/ serves its index.html" "sub index" "$BODY"

# --- 404 for unknown paths ----------------------------------------------------
check_status "GET /nope.txt -> 404"            "$BASE/nope.txt" 404
check_status "GET /nope/deeper -> 404"         "$BASE/nope/deeper" 404
check_status "GET /missing.png -> 404"         "$BASE/missing.png" 404
check_status "GET file outside root -> 404 (not served even if it exists)" \
             "$BASE/../outside-secret.txt" 404

# --- HEAD support -------------------------------------------------------------
HEAD_CODE=$(curl -s -I -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$BASE/index.html")
check "HEAD /index.html -> 200" 200 "$HEAD_CODE"
HEAD_TYPE=$(curl -s -I "$BASE/data.json" | tr -d '\r' | grep -i '^content-type:' | awk '{print $2}')
check "HEAD /data.json Content-Type" "application/json" "$HEAD_TYPE"
HEAD_LEN=$(curl -s -I "$BASE/data.json" | tr -d '\r' | grep -i '^content-length:' | awk '{print $2}')
if [ "${HEAD_LEN:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
  PASS=$((PASS + 1)); echo "ok:   HEAD /data.json has nonzero Content-Length ($HEAD_LEN)"
else
  FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); echo "FAIL: HEAD /data.json Content-Length not > 0: [$HEAD_LEN]"
fi
check_status "HEAD /nope -> 404" "$BASE/nope" 404 "-I"

# --- path traversal protection (all must be 403) ------------------------------
RAW="http://127.0.0.1:$PORT"
trav() {
  local desc="$1" target="$2"
  local code
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --path-as-is "$RAW$target")
  check "403: $desc" 403 "$code"
}
trav "/../.."                       "/../.."
trav "/../../etc/passwd"            "/../../etc/passwd"
trav "/%2e%2e"                      "/%2e%2e"
trav "/%2e%2e/"                     "/%2e%2e/"
trav "/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd"    "/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd"
trav "/..%2f..%2fetc/passwd"        "/..%2f..%2fetc/passwd"
trav "/%252e%252e (double-encoded)" "/%252e%252e/%252e%252e/etc/passwd"
trav "/....//"                      "/sub/../../outside-secret.txt"
# encoded traversal that decodes to something inside root but normalizes out
trav "/sub/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/outside-secret.txt" "/sub/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/outside-secret.txt"

# the secret really is outside root and must never be reachable
SECRET=$(curl -s --path-as-is "$RAW/%2e%2e/../outside-secret.txt")
check "secret file content never leaks" "" "$SECRET"

# --- summary ------------------------------------------------------------------
echo
echo "passed: $PASS  failed: $FAIL"
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]

## Summary

**`/workspace/serve.js`** — Node stdlib-only static server:
- `--port` (0 = ephemeral, actual bound port printed on startup) and `--root`
- Extension map: `.html → text/html`, `.css → text/css`, `.js → text/javascript`, `.json → application/json`, `.png → image/png`
- Directory requests serve `index.html` if present, otherwise a generated HTML listing
- 404 for unknown paths, HEAD support (correct status + `Content-Type` + `Content-Length`, no body)
- Traversal protection: URL-decodes the path, resolves against root with `path.resolve`, and returns **403** if the result escapes root — plus a second containment check on a twice-decoded form so `%2e%2e`, `..%2f..%2f`, and double-encoded `%252e%252e` are all rejected

One real bug surfaced during testing: an initial `path.posix.normalize('/' + '/..')` collapsed to `''`, silently mapping `/..` back onto the root itself and bypassing the check. Removing the redundant normalize (resolve already normalizes) fixed it.

**`/workspace/test.sh`** — builds a temp fixture tree, starts the server on port 0, parses the printed port, then asserts with `curl`:
- Status + `Content-Type` for all five mapped extensions
- Body equality for one file (`file.txt`) and for index serving
- Generated listing (`Index of …`, `text/html`) for an index-less directory; index preferred when it exists
- 404s for unknown files/deep paths and a file outside root
- HEAD status/type/length, plus HEAD 404
- Nine traversal variants (`/../..`, `/%2e%2e`, `/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd`, `..%2f..%2f`, double-encoded, etc.) all expecting 403, and a final assertion that the fixture's "secret" file content never leaks

It prints `ok:`/`FAIL:` per case, tallies pass/fail counts, and exits nonzero on any failure.
